ADAPT trial (NEJM 2021): 68% MG-ADL responders vs. 30% placebo. Treatment policy estimand (IgG reduction measured during dosing cycle). Q1W×4 cycles, restart when symptoms return. Market leader but cycling regimen is the primary patient inconvenience. ARGX-213 (next-gen extended half-life) is argenx's own admission that Q1W is insufficient long-term.

Vivacity-MG3 Ph3: positive gMG. IV Q2W continuous dosing — best approved dosing frequency. FDA approval Jan 2025. SC formulation in development. IgM/IgA preservation confirmed. Broadest indication pipeline in class. BD anchor: J&J validation of FcRn as a multi-billion dollar franchise.

MycarinG Ph3: positive gMG. SC Q1W self-administration (auto-injector). Approved 2023. Weekly SC is patient-convenient vs. IV but still Q1W burden. Validates SC route in gMG — de-risks Ailux SC administration target.
2026–2027 — Ph3 data in gMG, WAIHA, IgAN, SLE

IMVT-1402 (next-gen batoclimab): 74% IgG reduction at Q1W×4, 600mg cohort. No albumin depletion, no LDL elevation — clean profile. Phase 2/3 in multiple autoimmune indications. Sets the efficacy benchmark (≥70% IgG depletion) for Ailux to match at Q6–8W frequency.

Argenx's own acknowledgment that efgartigimod's Q1W×4 cycling is insufficient. ARGX-213 designed for extended half-life via Fc engineering — direct competitor to Ailux albumin VHH approach. IND expected 2026. Race to first extended-dosing FcRn inhibitor in clinic is underway.

2nd-round NHP studies: albumin flat/rising, LDL no elevation, IgG ≥70% depletion, Q6–8W interval. Architecture: FcRn inhibitor arm + albumin VHH binder (rides albumin's FcRn recycling). 4× less frequent than current best approved (Q2W nipocalimab). Off-the-shelf, SC target. IND-enabling studies to follow NHP.
